In the school lift, Charu hesitated. “Pranav, I have to tell you something. People are saying you copied in the maths test.” Pranav's ears went hot. “I didn't.” “I know. But it's on the class group.”

All day he watched faces. Two girls stopped talking when he passed. A boy in the corridor smirked. Pranav stared at his shoes and counted tiles. He couldn't tell who had started it; anyone might have.

At lunch he sat behind the library shelves for ten minutes, wishing he could vanish. When he came out, Charu was waiting. “I'll come with you to talk to Mrs. Kulkarni,” she said. “Right now.” “Now?” “Now.”

qa.q: Where did Charu tell Pranav about the rumour?
qa.a: Charu told Pranav about the rumour in the school lift.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling as watching faces all day?
qa.a: Pranav felt hot shame and fear of every glance, unable to tell who had started the story.

qa.q: What choice did Charu make that helped Pranav?
qa.a: Charu offered to go with Pranav to Mrs. Kulkarni right away.

qa.q: What might Charu have been feeling while telling Pranav about the rumour?
qa.a: Charu probably felt nervous and worried for Pranav but loyal enough to tell the truth.

grounding: A teenager learns that a false story about them is spreading, feels hot shame and fear of every glance, and cannot tell who started it.

passage:
Nikita, his older sister, sat on the edge of Akash's bed.

“Akash, you need to hear something.”

“What?”

“A girl from my tuition class says there's a story going round your school. That you copied a friend's homework and blamed someone else.”

“What? That's not true.” His voice cracked. “Who said that?”

“I don't know. It's just going round.”

“So everyone thinks...” Akash pulled the blanket up. “I can't go tomorrow. I'll just disappear.”

Mummy stood in the doorway holding a dishcloth. “Akash, come here. Whatever it is, tell me.” He told her everything. She listened, then took out her phone. “I'll call your class teacher tonight. And you're not walking in alone tomorrow.”

Nikita nodded. “I'll stand next to you at the gate.”

qa.q: Who will walk in with Akash tomorrow?
qa.a: Nikita will stand next to Akash at the gate and walk in with Akash.

qa.q: Why did Akash say he would just disappear?
qa.a: Akash felt shame and fear that everyone at school believed the false story, so hiding felt like the only escape.

qa.q: What did Mummy do the same evening?
qa.a: Mummy listened to Akash and said she would call the class teacher that night.

qa.q: What might Nikita have felt when delivering the news?
qa.a: Nikita probably felt worried and protective, unsure how Akash would react but wanting Akash to hear it from family.

grounding: A teenager learns that a false story about them is spreading, feels shame and a wish to disappear, and cannot tell who started it.
